stories.title: Three killed in strikes on Gaza as Israel renews threats over kite-flying
stories.summary: Israeli defence minister renews threat to expel Palestinians from any areas where kites or balloons are being flown in Gaza. At least three Palestinians have been killed in separate Israeli attacks on the Gaza Strip, medics and local media reported. This comes as Israel’s Defence Minister Israel Katz on Thursday renewed his threat to expel Palestinians from any area in Gaza where kites were being flown. One Palestinian was killed and others injured in an Israeli attack on a tent housing displaced people west of Gaza City on Thursday, a source at Al-Shifa Hospital said. An Israeli drone strike also hit a tent sheltering displaced people in the al-Mawasi area in western Khan Younis, killing one person and injuring others, the Palestinian Wafa news agency reported. Separately, an Israeli drone targeted an electric bicycle near the al-Sinaa intersection west of Gaza City, killing one person and injuring several others, including one critically, it added. The ongoing Israeli attacks come despite a US-brokered “ceasefire” that came into effect in October 2025. Although major fighting halted in the strip after the agreement, deadly Israeli strikes have continued. The Israeli military said the latest air strikes in Khan Younis were targeting Hamas fighters. In a post on X, it claimed that a Hamas commander who took part in holding three Israeli hostages was killed in the strikes. Palestinian authorities accuse Israel of undermining efforts to implement a broader plan by US President Donald Trump to end the genocidal war on Gaza, which includes the full withdrawal of Israeli troops from the strip and disarming Hamas. As strikes continue, Katz renewed his threat to expel Palestinians from areas where kites or balloons were being flown in Gaza.

stories.title: Abbas gives Pakistan edge with four wickets against England in second test
stories.summary: England battled back from 80-4 at lunch to 248-9 by the end of the rain-shortened first day at Lord’s. Pakistan bowler Mohammad Abbas took four wickets as his side edged the first day of the second Test against England at Lord’s Cricket Ground in London, although the hosts battled back from a rocky start to end a weather-shortened day on 248-9. After Pakistan won the toss and elected to bowl on a muggy Thursday morning following a rain delay, Abbas took full advantage of the conditions to wreck England’s top order. A stunning spell of three for 34 before lunch, including the removal of England captain Joe Root, put Pakistan in command, with the hosts reeling on 80-4 at lunch. But England, led by half-centuries for Jordan Cox and Jamie Smith, responded to move towards a respectable total, especially against a Pakistan side whose batting was ruthlessly exposed in a heavy defeat at Leeds. Cox dug in for 55 while Smith made an aggressive 61 as England recovered from 120-5. Gus Atkinson swung the bat late on for an unbeaten 34 before bad light forced an early close. The vastly experienced Abbas would have smiled when captain Babar Azam, back after missing the first Test defeat, called right to win a delayed toss. Eight years ago at Lord’s, Abbas claimed eight wickets in a Pakistan victory, and he found conditions to his liking again as he went about his business in skilful fashion. He made the breakthrough with the last ball of his third over when Emilio Gay tried to flick a leg-side ball off his pads but was caught by a diving Mohammad Rizwan behind the stumps. Ben Duckett looked to be aggressive, but was undone when on 17 as Abbas jagged a ball back that trapped him on his back foot. He was given out leg before wicket (LBW) on review.

stories.title: French presidential candidates clash at first debate before upcoming elections
stories.summary: Seven of France's leading candidates locked horns on Thursday in their first debate, eight months ahead of an increasingly tight and crowded election to succeed President Emmanuel Macron. The debate comes less than eight months ahead of the 2027 election to choose France's new leader, with centrist incumbent Macron having served the maximum two consecutive terms.

stories.title: The Falklands close the second Loligo squid season three days after reopening it
stories.summary: The Falkland Islands Fisheries Department announced on Thursday the closure of the second Loligo squid season due to low biomass levels, just three days after fishing had resumed following a two-week pause. “This decision has been taken as a result of analysis of the catch data following the resumption of fishing after the two-week pause, as well as the results of the two days of exploratory fishing,” the island government said in its statement. The text describes the measure as precautionary and aimed at ensuring the long-term sustainability of the fishery, adding that the department is already looking at what measures can be trialled or implemented ahead of the 2027 seasons to mitigate the problems recorded in the second season in recent years. The sequence was rapid. On August 12 the administration suspended activity within the Loligo Box over low biomass. Fishing resumed on the 24th and the season was closed on the 27th. According to the weekly Penguin News, the industry was advised only days after the resumption that levels remained very low. Director of Natural Resources James Wilson told the newspaper there were “very deep concerns” regarding the second season and pointed to several converging factors. He mentioned oceanographic currents that in 2024 swept the squid out of the area, with questions over how many later returned to the Loligo Box to breed. He also cited increasing numbers of predatory hake in the area, which he attributed most likely to closures in Argentine fishing grounds. And he added that pressure on the fishery has grown significantly even though the number of vessels has remained stable, because the boats are bigger and more powerful and both nets and fishing hours have changed. It is the fourth consecutive year of difficulties in the second season.

stories.title: Eduardo Coudet steps down as River Plate coach after Copa Sudamericana elimination
stories.summary: The news was confirmed on Thursday, along with the announcement that Leonardo Ponzio will serve as interim head coach La entrada Eduardo Coudet steps down as River Plate coach after Copa Sudamericana elimination se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald .
article_sentences: River Plate head coach Eduardo “Chacho” Coudet will step down from his post after the club was ousted from the Copa Sudamericana round of 16 against Colombia’s Independiente Santa Fe on Wednesday.
The news was confirmed Thursday in a press conference at the Monumental Stadium attended by Coudet, club president Stefano Di Carlo, and manager Enzo Francescoli.

“We didn’t have a good start to the second half of the year, and we knew from the start that things at River were unsustainable if results don’t go your way,” Coudet said, adding that he will continue to “root from the outside.” He also praised the team, saying that they will “win many championships for the club.”
Leonardo Ponzio will serve as interim head coach.
The Millonario, which just went through its worst start to a season since 1911 with five straight defeats, was eliminated on Wednesday on penalties 8-7 after tying 1-1 on aggregate.
Amidst a heated atmosphere at the Monumental Stadium, filled with jeers, insults, and whistles from the crowd, the game actually started River’s way.
Striker Sebastián Driussi put Coudet’s team ahead seven minutes into the second half, before Franco Fagúndez evened the scores from the penalty spot with ten minutes to go.
Millonario goalkeeper Santiago Beltrán saved three penalties in the shootout, but even that wasn’t enough for River.
With the chance to seal the win at 4-4, River’s Rafael Borré sent his shot against the post.
The shootout went to sudden death when Independiente goalkeeper Weibmar Asprilla secured the win for the Colombian side.
The heated atmosphere did not dissipate after the final whistle.
As soon as the match ended, club members and fans started pouring into the stadium’s central hall to protest Coudet’s tenure, chanting for the return of former River head coach Ramón Diaz.
